issues.legal_issue: Refusal of a properly sent registered demand notice constitutes effective service and imputes knowledge of its contents, so failure to pay the demanded rent within the applicable time may amount to wilful default.
material_facts: The tenant owed rent for earlier years and had not paid it.
The landlords sent a registered notice demanding arrears and seeking eviction, properly addressed and prepaid.
The postman testified that he tendered the notice to the tenant, who refused to accept it; the courts accepted that evidence.
The tenant did not pay the arrears within one month after the notice was tendered and refused.
issues.conclusion: The refusal amounted to effective service, and the tenant was imputed with knowledge of the notice’s contents. His failure to pay within one month was wilful default under Section 14(a) of the applicable Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 raises a rebuttable presumption of due service when a document required or authorised to be served by post is properly addressed, prepaid and sent by registered post. Section 114, Illustration (f), of the Evidence Act similarly permits a presumption that the ordinary course of postal business was followed. Effective service includes the contents of the notice, and an addressee who refuses a tendered notice is imputed with knowledge of those contents. The Court approved the Allahabad High Court decisions in Shri Nath v. Smt. Saraswati Devi Jaswal, Fanni Lal v. Smt. Chironja, and Ganga Ram v. Smt. Phulwati; it regarded the contrary observations in Vaman Vithal Kulkarni v. Khanderao Ram Rao Sholapurkar as obiter and not the correct legal position.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and notice_properly_sent_by_registered_post and notice_tendered_and_refused and postal_service_presumption_unrebutted and rent_unpaid_after_notice_deadline

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a rent-control proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant for failure to pay rent.
predicates.notice_properly_sent_by_registered_post: The landlord properly addressed, prepaid and sent a demand notice to the tenant by registered post.
predicates.notice_tendered_and_refused: The postal carrier tendered the notice to the tenant, and the tenant refused to accept it.
predicates.postal_service_presumption_unrebutted: The tenant did not establish facts that rebutted the presumption of proper postal service.
predicates.rent_unpaid_after_notice_deadline: The tenant did not pay the demanded arrears within the time allowed after service of the notice.
predicates.tenant_committed_wilful_rent_default: The tenant’s failure to pay the demanded rent after effective service of the notice constitutes wilful default.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding refuses a properly sent registered demand notice, the service presumption remains unrebutted, and the tenant does not pay by the notice deadline, the tenant has committed wilful rent default.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord does not need prior permission from the District Magistrate to bring an eviction suit on a ground expressly listed in the rent-control statute.
material_facts: The landlords brought an eviction suit on the ground of the tenant’s wilful failure to pay rent after a demand notice.
The landlords had not obtained the District Magistrate’s permission before filing the suit.
issues.conclusion: Permission was not required because the suit was brought on a ground specified in Section 14(1)(a); the Civil Court could entertain it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the U.P. Cantonments (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1952 requires the District Magistrate’s permission for an eviction suit only when the landlord relies on a ground other than those specified in clauses (a) to (f). Applying the interpretation of the materially identical provision in Section 3(1) of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, the Court relied on Bhagwan Dass v. Paras Nath.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_suit: A landlord filed a suit seeking eviction of a tenant under a rent-control law.
predicates.eviction_ground_is_statutorily_listed: The landlord relied on a ground that the rent-control law expressly lists as a basis for eviction.
predicates.prior_district_magistrate_permission_not: The landlord may bring the eviction suit without first obtaining permission from the District Magistrate.

issues.definition: A landlord bringing a rent-control eviction suit on an expressly listed eviction ground need not first obtain the District Magistrate’s permission.
